inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E net sales: 9M actual 5,835.3 (10-Q filed 2026-10-01) + Q4E ~2,125 (Q4 FY2025 1,850.4 x 1.15, inside the reaffirmed +13-17% FY2026 guide; McCormick de Mexico consolidated from 2026-01-02 so Q4 still carries the full acquisition step-up). FY2025 revenue (6,840.3) is NOT a comparable base because MdM was equity-accounted then.
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted, Q3 FY2026 10-Q income statement (269.4m; basic outstanding at 2026-08-31 = 14,522,864 voting + 254,541,615 non-voting = 269.06m). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. Dilution from the pending Unilever Foods RMT (legacy holders -> ~35.0%) is NOT in this count; see corporate_action.
inputs.net_debt_note: Balance sheet at 2026-08-31: short-term borrowings 1,340.2 + current portion of LTD 771.9 + long-term debt 2,906.1 = 5,018.2; cash 331.1. The DB total_debt (4,449.9) does not tie to the statement and is not used. Operating-lease liabilities (~227m, ASC 842) excluded: lease cost is already inside EBITDA (one lease treatment).
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 2026-08-31 from XBRL cash-flow statements: ShareBasedCompensation FY2025 46.2 - 9M FY2025 37.3 + 9M FY2026 34.5 = 43.4; PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation 13.2 - 13.2 + 11.9 = 11.9; combined 55.3 (no company-published combined figure, so the two lines are summed).
inputs.fcf_note: TTM to 2026-08-31: OCF 962.2 - 420.2 + 598.8 = 1,140.8; capex 221.8 - 138.1 + 131.2 = 214.9; reported FCF 925.9. TTM OCF is depressed by ~152m of Unilever transaction costs expensed in special charges and flattered by ~29m of IEEPA tariff refunds; both are one-offs and are not carried into the component build. Interest income (~30-40m/yr in Other income) is NOT stripped: the company is a net debtor, and the component build starts from EBITDA so non-operating income is excluded by construction.
inputs.buyback_note: 9M FY2026 repurchases 10.9m (FY2025 34.8m, FY2024 53.1m): repurchases roughly offset option exercises and the count has been flat at ~269m since FY2019. Flat count is funded, not a convention. Capital return is via the dividend (0.48/qtr, ~1.92/yr, ~517m/yr).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-01T20:00:02Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 43.94-72.41; price sits at the 52-week low
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate: 10y UST ~4.2%, ERP 5.0%, equity beta 0.8 (staples; raised from the historical ~0.6 for the pending levered combination) -> cost of equity 8.2%; pre-tax cost of debt 5.0% (4.15% 2029 notes issued Feb-2026, commercial paper ~5.25%) -> 3.8% after 24% tax; D/V ~30% at market (equity ~11.9bn, debt 5.0bn) -> 6.9%, rounded to 7.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios; scenario risk is carried in the flows and weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842 operating leases: lease cost (77.0m FY2025) is an operating expense inside EBITDA; lease liabilities excluded from net debt. Treatment (B), applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Grupo Herdez retains 25% of McCormick de Mexico (consolidated from 2026-01-02). Flows are modelled on 100% of consolidated EBITDA and the NCI is deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at its acquisition-date fair value carried on the balance sheet (583.8m at 2026-08-31; NCI income run-rate ~10m/qtr). Not folded into the tax rate as well.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (standalone consolidated McCormick incl. 75% of McCormick de Mexico). Routed as an operating consumer-staples company per dcf-methods SKILL.md; adaptations file read for the NCI (charged once in the bridge) and lease rules. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF). Q1 FY2026 GAAP net income of 1,022.3m contains an 866.8m non-cash remeasurement gain on the previously held 50% of McCormick de Mexico (Income from unconsolidated operations); it is excluded from every margin anchor here. CORPORATE ACTION: on 2026-03-31 McCormick signed a Reverse Morris Trust merger with Unilever's Foods business (Knorr, Hellmann's): legacy MKC holders -> ~35.0% of the combined company, Unilever holders 55.1%, Unilever retains up to 9.9%; 15.7bn cash paid to Unilever, funded by new debt (bridge/term loan/notes); close expected mid-2027 subject to the MKC shareholder vote and multi-jurisdiction antitrust; 420m termination fee in specified cases. The skill's routing says a live corporate action should be weighted deal-completes vs deal-breaks. The Drivers engine takes ONE revenue base / share count / net debt, so this file values the STANDALONE company (= the deal-breaks path, and the user's requested basis) and carries a hand-built deal-completes estimate and a deal-probability-weighted memo in `corporate_action`. Read the headline weighted_iv as the standalone value, and the `corporate_action.deal_weighted_iv_memo` as the value of a share held through the expected close. Margin anchors: 9M FY2026 adjusted operating margin 16.5% (Q3 17.7%), FY2026E adjusted OI ~1,300-1,340m (guide +16-20%), D&A 9M 213.1 -> FY ~285m (3.6%), SBC+equity taxes ~0.7% of sales. FY2026E pre-SBC EBITDA margin ~20.75%; FY2027 base path starts at 21.0%.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interest: Grupo Herdez 25% of McCormick de Mexico
equity_bridge.note: Balance sheet 2026-08-31, carried at acquisition-date fair value (Q3 FY2026 10-Q). NCI charged once, here, not in the tax rate.

Residual Income from unconsolidated operations runs ~3m/qtr (Q2-Q3 FY2026) and is excluded from the EBITDA build; matching asset added at ~8x that ~12m/yr. Book value is not separately disclosed in the 10-Q; conservative estimate.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management FY2026 organic guide (1-3%) plus McCormick de Mexico growth and pricing, cross-checked against revenue_5yr_cagr 4.1%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (7.9%/5yr) exceeds revenue CAGR (4.1%) by >30%: book growth is retained earnings on a 60-65% payout plus FX/pension OCI, not a growth proxy. Not used for growth selection.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs on FY2020->FY2025 and FY2022->FY2025 annual data (owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes: FY2020 757, FY2022 309.8, FY2025 681). The 3yr owner-FCF CAGR of +30% is a recovery from the FY2022 working-capital trough (inventory build) and is not repeatable; the 5yr owner-FCF CAGR is slightly negative while revenue compounded 4.1% and EPS ~1%: FY2020-25 was a period of commodity inflation, pricing catch-up and flat volumes. Owner-FCF CAGR (-2.1%) sits below reported (-1.9%) because SBC+withholding grew from 59m to 59m - essentially flat, so SBC is not eating the growth here.

base.narrative: Organic growth 3% (price 2%, volume/mix ~1% as MdM and APAC grow faster than the US Consumer core), decelerating to 2.5%. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin from ~20.75% (FY2026E) to 22% by year 6 on CCI savings and MdM accretion, then flat. D&A 3.6% / capex 3.4% (FY2023-25 capex averaged 3.7% incl. a DC build; FY2026 running ~2.5%). Cash tax 24% = guided FY2026 adjusted rate. Working capital consumes 10% of incremental revenue (AR 832 + inventory 1,446 - AP 1,481 = ~10% of sales). Terminal 2.5% g, capped at 18x year-10 FCF.

bull.narrative: Volume returns (+1-2%) on brand marketing and bold-flavor innovation, Flavor Solutions foodservice recovers, MdM grows high single digits in pesos; CCI plus mix lift the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 23%. Tax drifts to 23% as the mix shifts offshore. Terminal 3.0% g, capped at 20x.

bear.narrative: Private-label trade-down and retailer pushback cap price at ~1.5% with volume flat-to-down; commodity (pepper, garlic, vanilla) and freight inflation of 6-7% is only partly offset by CCI, pre-SBC EBITDA margin erodes to 19.5%; management attention is on the 15.7bn integration (or on a failed vote and 75-420m of break costs). Tax 25%. Terminal 2.0% g, capped at 15x.

scenario_narratives.base: Standalone McCormick as a 60%-share global spice leader with a newly controlled Mexican condiments platform: ~3% organic growth driven mostly by price, volumes roughly flat, gross margin expanding ~100bp on CCI, adjusted operating margin drifting from ~16.5% toward ~18% (pre-SBC EBITDA 21% -> 22%). The FY2026 guide (sales +13-17%, adj OI +16-20%, adj EPS 3.05-3.13, tax 24%) is taken at its midpoint for the FY0 anchor. The Q1 FY2026 866.8m remeasurement gain and the ~170m of FY2026 Unilever transaction costs are both excluded as one-offs.
scenario_narratives.bull: Volume growth returns as brand marketing (+low-to-mid-teens spend) and Flavor Solutions' QSR/foodservice recovery lift organic growth to 4-4.5%; McCormick de Mexico compounds high single digits; CCI and mix take the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 23%. The market re-rates a 23%-EBITDA-margin branded staple back toward its historical ~20x FCF.
scenario_narratives.bear: Value-seeking consumers and retailer consolidation push private label; price realisation falls to ~1.5% with flat-to-down volume; 6-7% input inflation (raised at Q3 FY2026) and Middle-East freight costs outrun CCI, compressing the margin ~1.5pp; the Unilever process absorbs management for two years (and, if the vote fails, costs 75m of reimbursement or, on a board change of recommendation, a 420m fee). A slow-growth, ex-growth staple capped at 15x FCF.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because (i) volumes have been flat for three years and FY2026 organic growth is price-only, (ii) input inflation guidance was raised to 6-7% at Q3, and (iii) the standalone business will be run for two years by a team whose priority is a 15.7bn integration, with break-fee exposure if the deal fails. Bull cut to 25% because the bull needs volume AND margin to turn simultaneously, which has not happened since FY2021. Weights sum to 1.0. These are STANDALONE weights; the deal-completes vs deal-breaks weighting lives in corporate_action.

corporate_action.type: Reverse Morris Trust merger with Unilever Foods (SpinCo 'Sandman Corporation')
corporate_action.source: 8-K filed 2026-04-01 (Item 1.01), Q3 FY2026 10-Q Note 2 and MD&A, Q3 FY2026 earnings release 2026-10-01
corporate_action.terms: Unilever separates its Foods business (ex India/Nepal/Portugal foods, Lifestyle & Nutrition, Buavita, Lipton RTD) into SpinCo; SpinCo pays Unilever 15.7bn cash (via asset sales/intercompany notes/SpinCo note, funded by McCormick's committed 15.7bn bridge, now partly replaced by a 2.0bn 3-year term loan and intended permanent notes); SpinCo merges into McCormick subsidiaries. Post-close ownership: Unilever shareholders ~55.1%, legacy McCormick shareholders ~35.0%, Unilever (via DutchCo) retains up to ~9.9% (or Unilever holders 65% if it distributes everything). Board 8 McCormick + 4 Unilever designees. McCormick to seek a European listing.
corporate_action.conditions_and_timing: MKC shareholder approval of the share issuance and charter amendment; S-4 effectiveness; HSR and other antitrust/foreign-investment approvals. Expected close mid-2027 (12-month outside date from 2026-03-31, two 6-month extensions). Termination fee 420m payable by McCormick on a board change of recommendation or a competing transaction; expense reimbursement up to 75m if shareholders vote no. Financing is not a closing condition.
corporate_action.management_pro_forma: Combined FY2025 revenue ~20bn, 21% operating margin; ~600m run-rate net cost synergies (two-thirds by year 2) plus ~100m to be reinvested; mid-to-high-single-digit adjusted EPS accretion in year 1, mid-to-high-teens by year 3.

deal_completes_estimate_per_legacy_share.method: Hand-built memo, NOT the engine: combined EBITDA x exit multiple - pro-forma net debt - NCI, divided by the post-close share count, expressed per legacy MKC share (legacy holders own 35.0%).
deal_completes_estimate_per_legacy_share.assumptions: Combined revenue ~21.1bn (20.0bn FY2025 basis per the release + ~1.1bn full-year McCormick de Mexico); 21% operating margin -> OI ~4.43bn; D&A ~3.4% -> EBITDA ~5.15bn pre-synergy, ~5.75bn with the 600m run-rate synergies. Pro-forma net debt ~20.9bn = McCormick 4.69bn + 15.7bn cash to Unilever + ~0.5bn fees/financing costs; Herdez NCI 0.58bn. Post-close shares = 269.4m / 0.35 = ~769.7m. Unilever Foods' own debt-like items, pension deficits and the final SDA working-capital/debt adjustments are unknown until the S-4/Form 10 and are excluded.
deal_completes_estimate_per_legacy_share.point_estimate_note: 11x EV/EBITDA on fully synergised EBITDA: between the 8-10x of large-cap US packaged food (GIS, KHC, CPB) and the 13-15x of MDLZ/HSY, for a 21%-margin flavour/condiments leader that will carry ~3.6-4.0x net leverage at close and must execute a 600m synergy programme. Leverage, synergy slippage and dis-synergies (retailer overlap in mustard/mayo) are the downside; multiple convergence toward McCormick's own historical 17-20x EBITDA is the upside.

corporate_action.probability_rationale: Signed definitive agreements, committed financing, regulatory filings submitted on schedule, integration office stood up, auditor changed for post-close independence. Residual risk: the MKC shareholder vote after a ~35% share-price fall since announcement (voting stock is concentrated in employee/insider hands, which helps), and antitrust remedies in condiments across the US/EU/LatAm. Set at 75%.
corporate_action.deal_weighted_iv_formula: 0.75 x 54.3 (deal-completes point estimate) + 0.25 x 58.23 (standalone probability_weighted.weighted_iv from the engine run of 2026-10-02) = 55.28
corporate_action.note: The headline weighted_iv in this file is the STANDALONE value (what a holder owns if the deal breaks, and the user's requested basis). A holder who keeps the shares through mid-2027 most likely ends up with 35% of the combined company; the deal-weighted memo is the value of that position. The market price near the 52-week low sits close to the deal-completes estimate at ~10x, i.e. the market is pricing the deal as near-certain and giving little credit for synergies.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on the standalone, consolidated McCormick (incl. 75% of McCormick de Mexico), SBC fully expensed and the share count held flat, 10-year component build at a 7% USD WACC with the terminal value capped at 15-20x year-10 FCF. The FY2026 base deliberately excludes the 866.8m non-cash MdM remeasurement gain, the ~170m of Unilever transaction costs and the ~29m tariff refund. The Herdez 25% NCI is deducted once in the bridge. Because a signed Reverse Morris Trust with Unilever Foods will, if completed in mid-2027, dilute legacy holders to ~35% of a ~21bn-revenue company carrying ~21bn of net debt, the file also carries a hand-built deal-completes estimate and a 75/25 deal-weighted memo; the standalone number is the deal-breaks leg of that weighting.
key_risks_to_valuation: Unilever Foods RMT closes (expected mid-2027): legacy holders are diluted to ~35.0%, consolidated net leverage rises to ~3.6-4.0x EBITDA, and value per legacy share depends on a 600m synergy programme and the multiple the market grants a levered food conglomerate (46.8-61.7 across 10-12x in the memo) rather than on this standalone model

Deal breaks: 75m expense reimbursement (failed vote) or 420m termination fee (board change of recommendation / competing bid), plus the ~75m of bridge fees already paid and ~2 years of management distraction
Volume: three years of flat-to-negative Consumer volume; FY2026 organic growth is price-only (1-3%), so any further private-label trade-down turns the base case into the bear
Input costs: FY2026 cost inflation raised to 6-7% (pepper, garlic, vanilla, freight via the Middle East); tariff policy remains a swing factor after the IEEPA refund
Discount-rate sensitivity: ~70% of value is terminal; at a 7% WACC the Gordon value (22.8x) exceeds the 18x cap, so the cap binds and value is a multiple call
McCormick de Mexico: 25% remains with Grupo Herdez; peso translation now a larger exposure; the 866.8m gain is a fair-value mark, not cash
